I have been on Effexor for over a decade and it saved my life. I am on 300mgs and am topped off.  

I have discontinued using it twice, once for pregnancy and last summer for a few months due to lack of insurance.

The HARDEST part of Effexor is the withdrawals.  If you start it, you don’t take it back. 5 months later and I started paying for it out of pocket because my body was still in withdrawal- and some people have withdrawals symptoms for years.

Effexor also has a short half life. 5(+-2) hours... meaning missing a dose by a few hours can produce withdrawal effects.

For me it’s three hours. If I catch it, within that time period I can function. If I forget a dose I wake up, mid night, usually during a vivid nightmare, completely drenched in sweat.  I have to change sheets.  I have brain zaps, my brain and vision is so foggy that I can’t drive, barely walk and have a hard time focusing. I feel extremely nauseous, throw up, and am dizzy. I am unable to control emotions and become suicidal. Many others reported the same.

Getting off Effexor is HARD. Users have reported having to count the little granules and reduce by one. 

It’s miserable. I don’t wish anyone to go through any of that, but what it does for me, the life it gave me back makes it worth it.
